title: Learning tunes from movies and his pitch sense
summary: He memorised tunes from early talking pictures, practised them in all keys, and can name notes only with an instrument in hand.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: Back to your early days, did you listen to records in those times?

Oh quite a bit. I used to go to the movie and hear a tune in a movie when the talking pictures first came out, and I tried to remember it until I got home and tried to remember the key that I heard it in, and tried to play it in that same key. Just more or less of a memory test. And then I tried to play it in all different kind of keys. The same tune until I more or less mastered it you'd say, you know, and then a key.
You got pretty near perfect pitch.
Well it's a funny thing, I can call out any key or any note if I have my instrument in my hand. Without it I can't.

That's just from training I think. I've trained myself that way. But if I hold my either clarinet or saxon I can tell you any note you're hitting without playing it myself. But to put the horn down I can't.
Would you take the clarinet to the movies with you?
No, no, that's why I used to try to remember from the time I got to the movies to the time
I got home. What bands did you listen to on records?
